thread_title: nice colors in Sarracenia montana Transylvania Co, NC
breadcrumb: nice colors in Sarracenia montana Transylvania Co, NC

posts.body_html: This winter, we've had some really nice sunshine, with mild day temperatures in the 60's and cool nights in the mid to low 30's. Such a combination has brought out some really nice colors in S. montana from Transylvania Co, NC. I've never seen these plants with so much color. Notice how dark the veins are in some of the pictures:

Thanks Eric! Yeah, I agree-these plants are definitely one of my favorites as well. It's pretty amazing to see all the diversity in the population as well-every clone is slightly different.

In the 4th picture, the way the hood curves in and forms a little hat-reminds me of that wacky S. rosea mutant called "smurf."

posts.body_html:
Here are some pics of S. montana F1 Transylvania Co, NC. These community pots were sorta neglected for a few years, but I pulled them out from the thick "forest" and gave them some blasting full sun. Here are the results! Pics taken 9/15/20-check out how Bulbophyllum ROUNDII that one trap is! Oh, don't waste your time google searching that word, just made it up....



nope! I didn't put a ball into the trap right after it opened just to make it look rounder, this is how the clone develops naturally!




late summer flower showed up in this pot due to heat stress. Nah, homies didn't pollinate it, those flowers don't have enough time around here to produce seeds, and there wasn't nuthin' to cross it with:
